_commissioner_comment: Runs the engine. Trades involving him are labelled in Section 10; the trade finder publishes all six pairs automatically (decided 2026-10-06).

yahoo._historical_league_keys_comment: Corrected Sep 2026. Eight of the nine were wrong, and had been since the first commit -- config said 380.l.23647 for 2017-18 where Yahoo's own team keys say 375.l.132631. The values here are derived from the league prefix of the team keys in data/historical/all_teams.json and RECORDS.team_name_history, which came from Yahoo pulls and agree with each other for every season; the game ids then form the real NBA sequence 375/385/395/402/410/418/428/454/466. verify_project_integrity re-checks this on every run.

league_structure._add_budget_comment: New for 2026-27: each team gets 3 adds a week, covering both the free pre-matchup window (12:01 AM on the matchup's first day until that day's first NBA tip) and mid-week adds posted in the group chat. There was NO add budget before 2026-27, so historical add counts are not violations of it. Trades do not cost an add: sync_transactions records both sides of a trade as an add, and those are marked '(via trade)' and excluded.
league_structure._rounds_comment: total_rounds = roster_size - il_slots and is fixed: you draft into every roster spot that is not an IL slot. keepers_per_team and total_draft_rounds describe the CURRENT season ONLY, and are meaningful only while every manager keeps the same number. From 2027-28 keeper counts differ by manager -- see keeper_rules and data_loader.keepers_for().

tiebreaker_rules._comment: Every tie the rules can produce, named. Anything not listed here RAISES -- code never guesses a tiebreak (Nick, 10-07). standings/fallback: regular-season standings, also the draft order and playoff seeding.
tiebreaker_rules._regular_season_week: A tied regular-season week is a T in the standings for both managers; nobody wins it. This follows Yahoo, which is how the league settles it (Nick, 10-20). Separate from series_week and cup_game on purpose.
tiebreaker_rules._tie_win_value: A T counts as this many wins for standings position: winning percentage is (W + 0.5*T) / (W + L + T), Yahoo's formula. A season series can end tied (e.g. 2-2-1); then head-to-head cannot separate the two and total points does.
tiebreaker_rules._series_week: A tied week inside a best-of-3 playoff series: the higher seed takes the week.
tiebreaker_rules._cup_game: A tied single game in the Cup: the higher (Cup) seed advances.
tiebreaker_rules._cup_seeding: Cup seeding tied on total points: the better regular-season finish gets the higher seed.

pre_data_era._note: The two seasons played before the current rules. Deliberately excluded from all_standings and RECORDS, deliberately still counted in the honour roll, so these are added to the nine-season derived totals to reconcile against LEAGUEHISTORY.xlsx. Key names match that file's columns exactly: titles_won is the regular season, playoff_championships is the bracket. They were previously named first_place_finishes and titles, where 'titles' meant playoff championships -- the opposite of what titles_won means one file over.

season._season_number_comment: Two counts, two scopes -- the same 11-vs-9 split as career honours. data_era_season_number: seasons with Yahoo data, 2017-18 on (this is the 10th); 'all-time' in the newsletter means this era. league_season_number: the whole league, counting 2014-15 and 2015-16 (records only, no stats; 2016-17 was not played) -- this is the 12th. Every consumer picks one explicitly; there is no plain season_number.
season._advice_comment: C2/C3 (Section 10 waiver plans and trade finder) publish from this report week, and only if the premise check (scripts/validate_marginal_value.py) is CLEAR for this season. Before it, and whenever the check is MARGINAL or FAIL, they run as a preview (output/advice_preview_weekN.html) and Section 10 is unchanged. MARGINAL means talk, not ship.

season_structure._comment: Per-season week layout. season.regular_season_weeks describes ONLY the current season; historical seasons varied and the engine must not assume one shape for all time. regular_through = last regular-season week. bracket = a postseason bracket was played.
season_structure._pre_yahoo: 2014-15 and 2015-16 predate usable Yahoo data and have no matchup records; their results live only in LEAGUEHISTORY.xlsx to-date totals. The league took 2016-17 off entirely.

2019-20.note: COVID stoppage; season ended wk19 with no bracket played

2020-21.note: 18-week season after the bubble; bracket in wks 17-18

2021-22.note: 22-week season (All-Star double week); bracket in wks 21-22

2026-27.note: new format: best-of-3 series wks 16-21 (semis 16-18, final and 3rd-place 19-21), cup wks 22-23

season_structure._derivation: THROUGH 2025-26 ONLY: the bracket was always the last two fantasy weeks, so regular_through = last_week - 2 whenever a bracket was played. The last week is not a fixed number because Yahoo stretches any week containing the All-Star break to 14 days, which changes how many fantasy weeks a season fits into; 2021-22 ran 22 weeks, not 23, so its bracket was weeks 21-22 and its regular season ended at week 20. That rule does NOT hold from 2026-27 onward -- see postseason_format, where the postseason is eight weeks long.

postseason_format._comment: The league format in force from effective_from onward. Earlier seasons played a two-week, single-game bracket in the final two weeks and are described individually in season_structure. All week ranges are inclusive [first, last].
postseason_format.name: three_stage

regular_season.title: League Champion
regular_season.decides: final standings, draft order, and payouts
regular_season.note: 5 meetings per opponent is deliberately odd so no season series can end drawn. 3 opponents x 5 = 15 weeks.

playoffs.title: Playoff Champion
playoffs.note: Every week of a series is played even after the series is decided, so a 2-0 series still plays its third week. The series winner is whoever wins the most of the three weeks.

cup.title: Cup Champion

rounds.name: Cup Third Place
rounds.note: Played and recorded for the stat history. Carries no stake (payouts.cup_third_place).

cup.prize: an extra (6th) keeper for the following season
cup.note: Single games, not series. The 2026-27 Cup is the first one ever played; its winner sets the 2027-28 keeper asymmetry.

simulations._season_sims: Simulations for every season-long simulator: title odds, playoff odds, Cup odds. ONE number on purpose (Nick, 10-20: don't split): the bracket simulators read the same keyed week matrices as title odds. Raised from 10,000 on 2026-10-21 (Nick): once untagged absences were simulated, 10,000 sims moved title odds up to 0.6 points between seeds; 50,000 holds them to about 0.3 and costs about 30 seconds.
simulations._marginal_value_sims: marginal_value (waiver, trade and keeper advice). Absences are persistent blocks, so one valuation's standard error at 400 sims was 15-20 points against C2's 10-point floor; at 3,000 a season-long add's is about 3.7. See claude/BASELINE_INJURY_RESULT_2026-10-21.md.
simulations._premise_trade_sample: scripts/validate_marginal_value.py samples this many one-for-one swaps per sample, in this many disjoint samples, instead of all 1,350 from both sides (25 minutes at 3,000 sims). The band must agree across samples or the gate records UNSTABLE (Nick, 10-21).
simulations._marginal_value_shortlist_sims: The advice pre-filter: every candidate is scored at this count and only the shortlist reaches marginal_value_sims. At 40 its noise was about 30 points -- a good add could be cut before the precise check ever saw it (Nick, 10-21). 200 costs about 45 s a weekly build.

durability_prior._comment: WHERE THE BASELINE HAZARD GETS player_proj_GP, and deliberately NOT the live data/PLAYERLIST.xlsx. The column changes meaning when the season starts: PRE-SEASON it is projected games out of 82 with a durability haircut on everyone (measured 2026-10-22 across all three stored snapshots: mean 69.1-69.3, sd 4.9-5.0, 31% of players within one game of the median), IN-SEASON it is games out of those REMAINING, marked down only for players Yahoo already knows are hurt (a fresh fetch the same day: mean 77.7, sd 2.74, 96% within one game of the median; GP correlates 0.52 against the stored file while FPPG correlates 0.97 -- only GP breaks). Taking it live in-season drops the hazard from about 16% to about 1.5% a game, which switches the injury model off and puts title odds back to Hayden at 78% (claude/HANDOFF_DURABILITY_PRIOR_2026-10-22.md).
durability_prior._which: The NEWEST PRE-SEASON snapshot, named here rather than inferred from a directory listing, so the prior cannot change under a run that did not ask it to. Scoring inputs (projectedFPPG, total projected FP) still come live from data/PLAYERLIST.xlsx -- those refresh correctly.
durability_prior._next_season: A new season sets this once, in the preseason checklist, to that season's first snapshot: take a PLAYERLIST before week 1 (py scripts/check_playerlist.py --snapshot) and point this key at it. verify_project_integrity FAILS when the file is missing, or when its GP column has lost its pre-season dispersion, or when it was taken after the season's first week started. PRESEASON_2026-27.md and SEASON_RESET.md say so.
durability_prior._flat_gp_share_max: Refuse a GP column with more than this share of players within one game of the median -- that is the in-season shape (96% today) rather than the pre-season one (31%). Used by scripts/check_playerlist.py and by the prior loader itself.

absence_chain._comment: Yahoo injury designations that drive the absence chain (modules/absence.py): P(he plays game k of his team's games from the tag's anchor | he missed every earlier one), for k = 1, 2, 3. The 2026-27 vocabulary is P, Q, D, O, OFS. P is healthy, OFS is a season-long out carried by absence_baseline (projected GP 0), and these three drive the chain.
absence_chain._stated: NICK'S STATED JUDGEMENT, NOT MEASURED. O and Q approved 2026-10-19 (as O and GTD, before Yahoo renamed GTD to Q); D added 2026-10-22, between Q and O at every game. Q's second game is deliberately LOWER than its first: a questionable player who then actually sat is in worse shape than the tag said.
absence_chain._calibration: Do not guess these from the historical log. It records is_injured, not the tag that was showing, and the tags it would have carried are the retired GTD/DTD vocabulary -- so measuring Q and D from it needs an assumption about how the old names map onto the new ones. That is a judgement for Nick, not a measurement (claude/HANDOFF_YAHOO_TAGS_2026-10-22.md sec.5).

absence_baseline._comment: Untagged absences (modules/absence.py, the baseline hazard). Every player misses games he is not tagged for: Yahoo's player_proj_GP is his projected GP over his team's REMAINING games, so his per-game miss rate is (remaining team games - projected GP) / remaining team games. Those misses come in BLOCKS, persistent within a simulated season: an absence is short (mostly one-game rests) or long (a real injury), chosen per absence; a healthy spell between absences is memoryless. The rate is not a parameter -- it is the projection. Only the block SHAPE lives here.
absence_baseline._nba_games_per_team: The NBA regular season. The schedule file lists 80 per team: the last 2 are set by the NBA Cup group stage and are added later. Yahoo projects GP over all 82, so the unscheduled games count as remaining when the rate is taken.
absence_baseline._measured: Fitted 2026-10-21 by maximum likelihood to every absence run in HISTORICAL_PLAYERLOG 2017-18..2025-26 (a team game with zero fantasy points while rostered; 2,805 complete runs plus 375 runs cut off by a roster move, treated as at-least-that-long). Two geometric components: 75% of absences average 1.24 games, 25% average 9.5. Mean absence 3.3 games. Re-fit with the same procedure; do not hand-tune these to hit the calibration bands.

keeper_rules._comment: Keeper counts are per-season and need NOT be uniform across managers. A manager's live picks = league_structure.total_rounds minus their keeper count, and keepers always occupy the LAST rounds. Any season after the last one listed in `seasons` inherits `default`.

2026-27.note: The last uniform year. Everyone keeps 6 (rounds 10-15) and drafts rounds 1-9, 36 live picks in all. No Cup had been played yet when these keepers were chosen.

default.note: The previous season's Cup winner keeps 6 (rounds 10-15) and drafts rounds 1-9; the other three keep 5 (rounds 11-15) and draft rounds 1-10. 39 live + 21 keeper = 60 = 15 rounds x 4 teams, so round 10 holds three picks rather than four.

cup_winners._comment: Season -> the manager who won that season's Cup (weeks 22-23). That manager keeps one extra player the FOLLOWING season. null means the Cup has not been played or the result has not been recorded yet; keepers_for() refuses to guess and treats every manager as base until it is filled in. scripts/start_new_season.py will not let a season be archived while its Cup winner is still null.

payouts._comment: Manager-to-manager payments; the league keeps no pot. USD.

league_champion.paid_by: 3rd and 4th place in the regular-season standings (weeks 1-15)

playoff_champion.paid_by: 3rd and 4th place in the playoff bracket, as decided by the weeks 19-21 third-place series

cup_champion.prize: one more keeper than the other three, the FOLLOWING season (keeper_rules: 2027-28 on, the previous season's Cup winner keeps 6, everyone else 5). Zero dollars; the only result that changes next season's rules.

playoff_third_place.note: The weeks 19-21 third-place series. Pride only FOR NOW: both semifinal losers pay the playoff champion regardless. If a stake is ever added, set it here -- the code reads it, nothing is hard-coded.

cup_third_place.note: The week-23 game between the Cup semifinal losers. Played and recorded; no stake.
